Determinants of Regional Electricity Shortages in India: A Multivariate Time Series Analysis (2015-2025)

Group 9

2026-02-25

1 Install and Load Libraries

# Run install block once if packages not yet installed
# install.packages(c("readxl","tidyverse","forecast","tseries","lmtest","FinTS","rugarch"))

library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(forecast)
library(tseries)
library(lmtest)
library(FinTS)
library(rugarch)

2 Load Data – All 36 States

# Update this path to your file location
# Or use: file_path = file.choose()
file_path = "C:/Users/Admin/Downloads/NMIMS Mumbai BA Docs/Trim 3/Time Series Analysis/State_Wise_Power_Dataset.xlsx"

month_map = c(Jan=1,Feb=2,Mar=3,Apr=4,May=5,Jun=6,
               Jul=7,Aug=8,Sep=9,Oct=10,Nov=11,Dec=12)

# Read all 36 sheets and combine
all_data = lapply(excel_sheets(file_path), function(s) {
  read_excel(file_path, sheet = s)
}) %>%
  bind_rows() %>%
  mutate(Month_Num = month_map[Month],
         Date = as.Date(paste(Year, Month_Num, "01", sep = "-"))) %>%
  arrange(Region, Date)

# Compute All-India monthly averages across all 36 states
india_avg = all_data %>%
  group_by(Year, Month_Num) %>%
  summarise(
    Shortage = mean(Shortage_Percent,              na.rm = TRUE),
    Coal     = mean(Coal_Stock_Days,               na.rm = TRUE),
    ATC      = mean(ATC_Loss_Percent,              na.rm = TRUE),
    PLF      = mean(Plant_Load_Factor_Percent,     na.rm = TRUE),
    RE       = mean(Renewable_Energy_Share_Percent, na.rm = TRUE),
    Nifty    = mean(Nifty_Energy_Return_Percent,   na.rm = TRUE),
    Temp     = mean(Avg_Temperature_Index,          na.rm = TRUE),
    Import   = mean(`Import_Dependency_%`,          na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year, Month_Num)

# Create time series objects
shortage = ts(india_avg$Shortage, start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
coal     = ts(india_avg$Coal,     start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
atc      = ts(india_avg$ATC,      start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
plf      = ts(india_avg$PLF,      start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
re       = ts(india_avg$RE,       start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
nifty    = ts(india_avg$Nifty,    start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
temp     = ts(india_avg$Temp,     start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)
imports  = ts(india_avg$Import,   start = c(2015,1), frequency = 12)

par(mfrow = c(1,1))
# Bar chart across all 36 states
all_data %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  summarise(Avg = mean(Shortage_Percent, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Region, Avg), y = Avg,

4 Time Series Decomposition

4.1 Seasonal Plot

ggseasonplot(shortage, year.labels = TRUE) +
  ggtitle("Seasonal Plot - All-India Shortage % by Month and Year") +
  theme_minimal()

Seasonal Plot - All-India Shortage % by Month

4.2 Additive Decomposition

Model: Observed = Trend + Seasonal + Irregular

decomp_add = decompose(shortage, type = "additive")
plot(decomp_add)

Additive Decomposition - All-India Shortage %

4.3 Multiplicative Decomposition

Model: Observed = Trend x Seasonal x Irregular

decomp_mult = decompose(shortage, type = "multiplicative")
plot(decomp_mult)

Multiplicative Decomposition - All-India Shortage %

4.4 STL Decomposition

stl_result = stl(shortage, s.window = "periodic")
plot(stl_result, main = "STL Decomposition - All-India Shortage %")

STL Decomposition - All-India Shortage %

4.5 Dominant Component

data.frame(
  Component = c("Trend", "Seasonal", "Irregular"),
  Variance  = round(c(
    var(na.omit(decomp_add$trend)),
    var(na.omit(decomp_add$seasonal)),
    var(na.omit(decomp_add$random))
  ), 4)
)
##   Component Variance
## 1     Trend   1.9967
## 2  Seasonal   0.0066
## 3 Irregular   0.3244

5 Smoothing Methods + MAD / MSE

5.1 Moving Averages

ma3  = ma(shortage, order = 3)
ma6  = ma(shortage, order = 6)
ma12 = ma(shortage, order = 12)

plot(shortage, main = "Moving Averages - All-India Shortage %",
     col = "grey50", lwd = 1.5)
lines(ma3,  col = "blue",   lwd = 2)
lines(ma6,  col = "red",    lwd = 2)
lines(ma12, col = "green4", lwd = 2)
legend("topright",
       legend = c("Actual","MA(3)","MA(6)","MA(12)"),
       col    = c("grey50","blue","red","green4"), lty = 1)

Moving Averages - All-India Shortage %

5.2 Simple Exponential Smoothing

ses_fit = ses(shortage, h = 12)
plot(ses_fit, main = "SES Forecast - All-India Shortage %")

SES Forecast - All-India Shortage %

5.3 MAD and MSE Comparison

actual = as.numeric(shortage)

data.frame(
  Method = c("MA(3)", "MA(6)", "MA(12)", "SES"),
  MAD    = round(c(
    mean(abs(actual - as.numeric(ma3)),                    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(abs(actual - as.numeric(ma6)),                    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(abs(actual - as.numeric(ma12)),                   na.rm = TRUE),
    mean(abs(actual - as.numeric(fitted(ses_fit))),        na.rm = TRUE)
  ), 3),
  MSE    = round(c(
    mean((actual - as.numeric(ma3))^2,                     na.rm = TRUE),
    mean((actual - as.numeric(ma6))^2,                     na.rm = TRUE),
    mean((actual - as.numeric(ma12))^2,                    na.rm = TRUE),
    mean((actual - as.numeric(fitted(ses_fit)))^2,         na.rm = TRUE)
  ), 3)
)
##   Method   MAD   MSE
## 1  MA(3) 0.199 0.084
## 2  MA(6) 0.279 0.178
## 3 MA(12) 0.370 0.328
## 4    SES 0.343 0.345

5.4 Trend Forecasting Numerical

Data: 120, 135, 150, 165, 140, 155, 170, 185 — Forecast Period

values      = c(120, 135, 150, 165, 140, 155, 170, 185)
time_period = 1:8
trend_model = lm(values ~ time_period)

# Model summary
summary(trend_model)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = values ~ time_period)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -16.191  -7.143   0.000   7.143  16.191 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)  119.286      8.781  13.585 9.87e-06 ***
## time_period    7.381      1.739   4.245  0.00541 ** 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 11.27 on 6 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.7502, Adjusted R-squared:  0.7086 
## F-statistic: 18.02 on 1 and 6 DF,  p-value: 0.005411
# Forecast period 9
fc9 = predict(trend_model, newdata = data.frame(time_period = 9))
cat("Forecast for Period 9:", round(fc9, 2), "/n")
## Forecast for Period 9: 185.71 /n
# Plot
plot(time_period, values, type = "b", pch = 16, col = "blue",
     xlim = c(1,9), ylim = c(100, 210),
     main = "Trend Forecast", xlab = "Period", ylab = "Value")
abline(trend_model, col = "red", lty = 2)
points(9, fc9, pch = 17, col = "red", cex = 2)
legend("topleft", legend = c("Actual","Trend Line","Forecast"),
       col = c("blue","red","red"), lty = c(1,2,NA), pch = c(16,NA,17))

6 Stationarity Tests

6.1 ACF and PACF

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
acf(shortage,  lag.max = 24, main = "ACF - Level")
pacf(shortage, lag.max = 24, main = "PACF - Level")

ACF and PACF - All-India Shortage (Level) 

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

6.2 ADF Test

H0: Series has a unit root (non-stationary). p < 0.05 = stationary.
ADF vs DF: ADF adds lagged difference terms to correct for serial correlation in residuals — this is the key distinction (Q13).

adf.test(shortage)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  shortage
## Dickey-Fuller = -1.9302, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.6055
## alternative hypothesis: stationary

6.3 KPSS Test

H0: Series is stationary. p < 0.05 = non-stationary.

kpss.test(shortage)
## 
##  KPSS Test for Level Stationarity
## 
## data:  shortage
## KPSS Level = 0.44573, Truncation lag parameter = 4, p-value = 0.05744

6.4 Phillips-Perron Test

pp.test(shortage)
## 
##  Phillips-Perron Unit Root Test
## 
## data:  shortage
## Dickey-Fuller Z(alpha) = -8.9676, Truncation lag parameter = 4, p-value
## = 0.5984
## alternative hypothesis: stationary

6.5 First Difference

shortage_d1 = diff(shortage)
adf.test(shortage_d1)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  shortage_d1
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.5796, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
acf(shortage_d1,  lag.max = 24, main = "ACF - After Differencing")
pacf(shortage_d1, lag.max = 24, main = "PACF - After Differencing")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
ndiffs(shortage)
## [1] 1

7 AR Models

7.1 Manual AR(1) Forecast

Model: X_t = 0.3 * X_{t-1} + 2, X11 = 13 → Forecast X12

# Manual calculation
phi   = 0.3
const = 2
X11   = 13
X12_hat = phi * X11 + const
cat("X_hat(12|11) =", phi, "x", X11, "+", const, "=", X12_hat, "/n")
## X_hat(12|11) = 0.3 x 13 + 2 = 5.9 /n

7.2 AR(1) as Infinite MA Weights

weight_table = data.frame(
  Lag    = 0:10,
  Weight = round(0.3^(0:10), 5)
)
print(weight_table)
##    Lag  Weight
## 1    0 1.00000
## 2    1 0.30000
## 3    2 0.09000
## 4    3 0.02700
## 5    4 0.00810
## 6    5 0.00243
## 7    6 0.00073
## 8    7 0.00022
## 9    8 0.00007
## 10   9 0.00002
## 11  10 0.00001
plot(0:10, 0.3^(0:10), type = "h", lwd = 3, col = "steelblue",
     main = "AR(1) as Infinite MA - Decaying Weights (phi=0.3)",
     xlab = "Lag k", ylab = "Weight (0.3^k)")
abline(h = 0, col = "grey")

7.3 Stationary vs Non-Stationary AR(1)

set.seed(42)
ar_stat    = arima.sim(model = list(ar = 0.5), n = 100)
ar_nonstat = ts(cumsum(rnorm(100)))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(ar_stat,    main = "rho=0.5 (Stationary)",     col = "blue")
plot(ar_nonstat, main = "rho=1.0 (Non-Stationary)", col = "red")

rho=0.5 vs rho=1.0 

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
cat("--- ADF on rho=0.5 ---/n")
## --- ADF on rho=0.5 ---/n
adf.test(ar_stat)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  ar_stat
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.808, Lag order = 4, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- ADF on rho=1.0 ---/n")
## --- ADF on rho=1.0 ---/n
adf.test(ar_nonstat)
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  ar_nonstat
## Dickey-Fuller = -2.4853, Lag order = 4, p-value = 0.3756
## alternative hypothesis: stationary

7.4 Fit AR Models on All-India Data

ar1 = Arima(shortage, order = c(1,0,0))
ar2 = Arima(shortage, order = c(2,0,0))
ar3 = Arima(shortage, order = c(3,0,0))

# AIC / BIC comparison
data.frame(
  Model = c("AR(1)","AR(2)","AR(3)"),
  AIC   = round(c(AIC(ar1), AIC(ar2), AIC(ar3)), 2),
  BIC   = round(c(BIC(ar1), BIC(ar2), BIC(ar3)), 2)
)
##   Model    AIC    BIC
## 1 AR(1) 238.21 246.86
## 2 AR(2) 240.00 251.53
## 3 AR(3) 241.60 256.02
checkresiduals(ar1)

AR(1) Residual Diagnostics 

## 
##  Ljung-Box test
## 
## data:  Residuals from ARIMA(1,0,0) with non-zero mean
## Q* = 38.972, df = 23, p-value = 0.01998
## 
## Model df: 1.   Total lags used: 24
plot(forecast(ar1, h = 12),
     main = "AR(1) Forecast - All-India Shortage %")

AR(1) 12-Month Forecast - All-India Shortage %

10.1 Volatility Clustering

nifty_clean = na.omit(nifty)

par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(3,4,2,1))

     col = "blue", ylab = "Return %")

     col = "red", ylab = "Squared Return")

Q11: Volatility Clustering - Nifty Energy Returns 

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

10.2 ARCH LM Test

H0: No ARCH effects. p < 0.05 = ARCH effects present → ARIMA alone is insufficient.

ArchTest(nifty_clean, lags = 6)
## 
##  ARCH LM-test; Null hypothesis: no ARCH effects
## 
## data:  nifty_clean
## Chi-squared = 112.33, df = 6, p-value < 2.2e-16

10.3 ARCH(1) Model

Model: h_t = alpha_0 + alpha_1 * e_{t-1}^2
alpha_1 = how strongly last period’s shock affects today’s variance (Q12)

arch1 = ugarchfit(
  spec = ugarchspec(
    variance.model     = list(model = "sGARCH", garchOrder = c(1,0)),
    mean.model         = list(armaOrder = c(1,0)),
    distribution.model = "norm"),
  data   = nifty_clean,
  solver = "hybrid")

show(arch1)

11 GARCH Models

Model: h_t = omega + alpha * e_{t-1}^2 + beta * h_{t-1}

12 Cointegration Pre-Check + ECM

12.1 ADF on Each Variable

Both variables must be I(1) — individually non-stationary but stationary after differencing — for cointegration to apply.

cat("--- Shortage ---/n");  adf.test(shortage)
## --- Shortage ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  shortage
## Dickey-Fuller = -1.9302, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.6055
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- Coal ---/n");      adf.test(coal)
## --- Coal ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  coal
## Dickey-Fuller = -1.6851, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.7074
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- ATC Loss ---/n");  adf.test(atc)
## --- ATC Loss ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  atc
## Dickey-Fuller = -6.5313, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- PLF ---/n");       adf.test(plf)
## --- PLF ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  plf
## Dickey-Fuller = -2.2504, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.4724
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- RE Share ---/n");  adf.test(re)
## --- RE Share ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  re
## Dickey-Fuller = -8.1286, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- Shortage (1st diff) ---/n"); adf.test(diff(shortage))
## --- Shortage (1st diff) ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  diff(shortage)
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.5796, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
cat("--- Coal (1st diff) ---/n");     adf.test(diff(coal))
## --- Coal (1st diff) ---/n
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  diff(coal)
## Dickey-Fuller = -5.1391, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary

12.2 Error Correction Model

12.2.1 Step 1 - Long-Run Regression

long_run = lm(as.numeric(shortage) ~ as.numeric(coal))
summary(long_run)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = as.numeric(shortage) ~ as.numeric(coal))
## 
## Residuals:
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -0.90101 -0.24005  0.00138  0.26920  0.93835 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                   Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)      10.249325   0.122057   83.97   <2e-16 ***
## as.numeric(coal) -0.367146   0.007837  -46.85   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.3688 on 130 degrees of freedom
## Multiple R-squared:  0.9441, Adjusted R-squared:  0.9436 
## F-statistic:  2195 on 1 and 130 DF,  p-value: < 2.2e-16

12.2.2 Step 2 - Test Residuals for Stationarity (Confirms Cointegration)

ecm_resid = residuals(long_run)
adf.test(ts(ecm_resid))
## 
##  Augmented Dickey-Fuller Test
## 
## data:  ts(ecm_resid)
## Dickey-Fuller = -4.3704, Lag order = 5, p-value = 0.01
## alternative hypothesis: stationary
plot(ts(ecm_resid),
     main = "ECM Residuals - Long-Run Equilibrium Error (All-India)",
     col  = "darkblue", ylab = "Residual")
abline(h = 0, col = "red", lty = 2)

Q18: ECM Residuals - Long-Run Equilibrium Error

12.2.3 Step 3 - Short-Run ECM

d_shortage = diff(as.numeric(shortage))
d_coal     = diff(as.numeric(coal))
ecm_lag    = ecm_resid[-length(ecm_resid)]

ecm_model = lm(d_shortage ~ d_coal + ecm_lag)
summary(ecm_model)

Interpretation: The coefficient on ecm_lag is the speed of adjustment.
A negative and significant value confirms that deviations from the long-run shortage-coal equilibrium are corrected each month — the hallmark of a genuine cointegrating relationship (Q18).
